Expanding Double Brackets AQA KS3 · Year 8 · Foundation
To expand double brackets, multiply every term in the first bracket by every term in the second bracket. You can use the FOIL method (First, Outside, Inside, Last) or the grid method to organise your working. Then collect like terms to simplify.

Method

1 Multiply each term in the first bracket by each term in the second2 Write each product in its grid cell3 Collect like terms (the two middle terms)4 Write the simplified answer5 Check by substituting a value

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the last term: you must multiply the constant in the first bracket by the constant in the second.
  • Sign errors with negatives: remember that a negative times a negative gives a positive.
  • Writing x + x instead of 2x for the middle term when collecting like terms.
  • Forgetting that x × x = x², not 2x.

Worked example

Expand and simplify: (x + 2)(x + 3)
Step 1 — Draw the grid with (x + 2) down the side and (x + 3) along the top.
Step 2 — Fill in: x·x = x², x·3 = 3x, 2·x = 2x, 2·3 = 6
Step 3 — Collect like terms: 3x + 2x = 5x
Step 4 — Write the answer: x² + 5x + 6
Check (x = 10): (10+2)(10+3) = 12×13 = 156 and 100+50+6 = 156 ✓

Visual aid — grid method

Grid model showing (x+2)(x+3): top row x times x gives x squared, x times +3 gives 3x; bottom row +2 times x gives 2x, +2 times +3 gives 6. Collecting like terms: x squared + 3x + 2x + 6 = x squared + 5x + 6.

Each cell shows the product of its row and column headers: (x+2)(x+3) = x² + 5x + 6.
